question: Investigate the largest negative account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 profit change. Compare corresponding months across the quarters and identify the biggest contributing month.

run.question: Investigate the largest negative account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 profit change. Compare corresponding months across the quarters and identify the biggest contributing month.

analysis.summary: COGS is the largest negative account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 operating-profit change. Comparing corresponding months, the March-to-June pair is the biggest COGS increase and therefore the biggest monthly drag among the matched pairs.

findings.text: COGS was the largest negative account contribution in the Q1-to-Q2 profit bridge; operating expenses were also negative, but less adverse.

Among corresponding-month comparisons, March to June had the largest COGS increase, exceeding the January-to-April and February-to-May increases. June is therefore the biggest contributing Q2 month, paired with March in Q1.
Q1 and Q2 are complete, with all six underlying months available for the comparison.

limitations: This identifies an accounting contribution, not the business cause of the COGS increase; the dataset contains no supplier, pricing, volume, mix, or staffing evidence.
suggested_questions: Would you like the corresponding-month revenue and operating-expense comparisons as context for the COGS movement?

result.name: Cobalt Services
conventions: Margins use aggregate profits divided by aggregate revenue.
Missing periods and nonpositive ratio denominators return null.
Percentage changes require a positive baseline.
Only financial aggregates are available. No customer, supplier, price, volume or staffing evidence exists.

arguments.summary: COGS is the largest negative account contribution to the Q1-to-Q2 operating-profit change. Comparing corresponding months, the March-to-June pair is the biggest COGS increase and therefore the biggest monthly drag among the matched pairs.

findings.text: COGS was the largest negative account contribution in the Q1-to-Q2 profit bridge; operating expenses were also negative, but less adverse.

Among corresponding-month comparisons, March to June had the largest COGS increase, exceeding the January-to-April and February-to-May increases. June is therefore the biggest contributing Q2 month, paired with March in Q1.
Q1 and Q2 are complete, with all six underlying months available for the comparison.

limitations: This identifies an accounting contribution, not the business cause of the COGS increase; the dataset contains no supplier, pricing, volume, mix, or staffing evidence.
suggested_questions: Would you like the corresponding-month revenue and operating-expense comparisons as context for the COGS movement?
